title: Image-test mapping-square comparison for cocartesian edges
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent Hom bifunctors and whole-square equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality], [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] and [lem-coef-kan-nerve-pullback-recognition], and the cocartesian mapping criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. Let $p:E\to B$ and $q:F\to B$ be inner fibrations of small quasicategories, and let $T:E\to F$ be fully faithful with $qT=p$. If $e:a\to b$ is $p$-cocartesian, then for every vertex $z\in E$ the coherent comparison of the criterion square for $e$ at $z$ with the criterion square for $T(e)$ at $Tz$ is an equivalence of whole square diagrams; in particular, the latter square is a homotopy pullback.

source.place: The image-test part of the returned simplex-inverse marking step: full faithfulness over a common base identifies the two top mapping spaces, coherent Hom functoriality supplies the square comparison, and whole-square pullback invariance transfers the criterion.

proof.text: Fix $z\in E$ and write $S_E$ for the criterion square with corners $\operatorname{Map}_E(b,z)$, $\operatorname{Map}_E(a,z)$, $\operatorname{Map}_B(p(b),p(z))$, $\operatorname{Map}_B(p(a),p(z))$, in that order. Write $S_F$ for the square obtained by replacing $(E,p,e,z)$ by $(F,q,T(e),Tz)$. Their bottom rows agree because $qT=p$, including the edge $qT(e)=p(e)$. By [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality], the top rows are restrictions of the coherent Hom bifunctors to the edge $e$ in the contravariant variable and the constant target $z$, or to $T(e)$ and $Tz$. The induced coherent Hom transformation $T_*$ restricts to a transformation between these top rows whose components are the maps induced by $T$ on the two right-pinched mapping spaces. The vertical maps are induced by $p$ or $q$. This specifies the four components of the desired square comparison: $T_*$ at $(b,z)$ and $(a,z)$ above, and identity maps on the two base mapping spaces below.

source.place: Corollary 8.3.5.8 and Remark 8.3.5.9 (03PD); restriction of coherent Hom functoriality to the edge and the fixed target. Agent specialization.

proof.text: We check compatibility with the specified commutation data, so that these components define $\eta:S_E\to S_F$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(N([1]\times[1]),\mathcal S)$. Use the fixed-edge roof and its triangle witness of [lem-coef-infinity-fixed-edge-prism-coherence]. Apply that statement to the functors $p$, $q$ and $T$. Every map between the roof spaces is postcomposition of a simplex by the indicated functor. Restriction to a face and precomposition with its displayed prism map commute with postcomposition: $T(t\circ v)=(Tt)\circ v$ for every simplex $t$ and indexing map $v$. Furthermore $q(Tt)=pt$ as simplices, by the equality of simplicial maps $qT=p$. Thus the diagrams of roof spaces commute strictly, both for the face maps $r_0,r_1$ and for the triangle witnesses $e(t)$. The bottom roof is identical in the two diagrams. The cited lemma identifies these roofs, including those triangle witnesses and the vertical maps, with the canonical precomposition squares. Consequently their comparison presents precisely $\eta$ with the top-row Hom transformation of step 1; all of the commutation data are retained. This is a specialization of the cited natural prism construction, not a choice of homotopies between four unrelated edge classes.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3, dual mapping-square presentation; the simultaneous functorial prism comparison is written out from the cited existing lemma.

proof.text: Full faithfulness means, by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], that the maps on the right-pinched mapping simplicial sets are weak homotopy equivalences. Hence the two top components of $\eta$, on $\operatorname{Map}_E(b,z)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_E(a,z)$, are equivalences of spaces. The two bottom components are identities, and so are equivalences too. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] with $K=N([1]\times[1])$ and target $\mathcal S$. Its four vertex tests are exactly these four components. It follows that $\eta$ is an equivalence of whole coherent square diagrams, proving the first assertion for this $z$. The construction works for every vertex $z$ of $E$.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.4.4, applied to the square indexing simplicial set; full faithfulness is the existing definition.

proof.text: Since $p$ is an inner fibration of quasicategories and $e$ is $p$-cocartesian, [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] says that $S_E$ is a homotopy pullback. By [lem-coef-kan-nerve-pullback-recognition], this is equivalent to $S_E$ being cartesian as a coherent square of spaces, with its specified commutation datum. That same lemma says that an equivalence of whole square diagrams preserves and reflects cartesianness. Apply it to the equivalence $\eta$ from step 3, and then its specified-homotopy recognition clause to $S_F$. The result is that $S_F$ is a homotopy pullback, as asserted. Only the tests at $Tz$ are claimed. No essential-surjectivity hypothesis or test at vertices of $F$ outside the image is used.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3, opposite dual; transfer using the cited whole-square pullback-recognition statement. Agent argument.

lean.note: States the fully faithful-over-the-base comparison of the complete cocartesian mapping criterion squares. Both roof maps gE, gF are fixed by their inclusion equations (postcomposition by p, q on whole triangles), the T-induced top comparison a is fixed by its inclusion equation and is a weak equivalence together with arrowSpaceMap T x z, the square presentations carry the canonical strict commutation, the whole squares are naturally equivalent, and the canonical image square at Tz is a homotopy pullback. Reviewer fix: gF and the commutation paths were previously unconstrained existentials.
